title: Final Project — Small Company Server
lead: Combine everything on one server: users, shared directory, web site, firewall, backup, timer, and a verified delivery report.
objectives: You plan the whole server first and take a VM snapshot before you change anything.
You build users alice, bob, carol, the groups staff and admins, and a shared directory /srv/company with setgid.
You publish a site with nginx, label it correctly (SELinux) or check AppArmor, and open ports 80/443 without locking yourself out of SSH.
You automate a backup with a script and a systemd timer.
You verify every step with a checklist and write a delivery report.

sections.title: 1. Plan and safety first
body: The target: a small company server called `linux-lab`. Three people work on it: **alice** (admin), **bob** and **carol**. Everything lives under `/srv/company`: `shared` (team files), `admin` (admins only), `web` (the site), `backup` and `scripts`.

**Work in the VM, never on a production machine.** This project creates users, changes permissions, SELinux labels, firewall rules and systemd units. Before you start, take a **snapshot** (module 0.2). If a step goes wrong you roll back in seconds.

The built-in terminal cannot run `useradd`, `nginx`, `firewall-cmd` or `systemctl`. So the simulator tasks rebuild the **files** of the project (permission tree, script, unit files, report) under `~/srv/company`, while the VM tasks do the real thing in `/srv/company`.
Order of work: 1) plan + snapshot, 2) users and directories, 3) web, 4) firewall, 5) backup + timer, 6) verify + report. RHEL/Rocky and Debian/Ubuntu differ in only a few commands; both are shown.

commands.what: Shows distribution name and version.
commands.where: Before you choose dnf or apt commands.
commands.why: Tells you which variant of the guide applies.

commands.what: Prints the SELinux mode: Enforcing, Permissive or Disabled.
commands.why: You must know the mode before testing the web label; keep it Enforcing.

commands.what: Shows which AppArmor profiles are loaded and in which mode.
commands.why: Ubuntu uses AppArmor instead of SELinux; here you only check it.

commands.what: Shows user id and group memberships.
commands.where: When you check who may use the shared directory.
commands.why: Group membership decides access to `/srv/company/shared`.

sections.warn: Take a VM snapshot now and name it `before-company-project`. Do not run this project on a real server that others use.
sections.tip: Keep a notes file while you work. Every command you run becomes a line in your delivery report later.

sections.title: 2. Users, groups and the shared directory
body: Create the groups `staff` (alice, bob, carol) and `admins` (alice only). Use `useradd -m -G` for the users. Deleting users is **not** part of this project (`userdel -r` would remove home directories).

A shared directory needs two things. **Setgid** (`chmod 2770`) makes new files inherit the directory group `staff`, so bob can edit carol's files. Mode `770` keeps everybody else out. Optionally add a **default ACL** (`setfacl -d -m g:staff:rwx`) so new files are group-writable even with a strict umask.

Use least privilege: `web` is `755` (nginx must read it), `scripts` is `750`, `backup` is `700`. In the simulator you practise the same modes with `chmod` on `~/srv/company`; a normal user cannot `chgrp` there, so the group part is VM only.

commands.what: Creates a user with home directory, shell and extra group.
commands.where: Once for each of alice, bob, carol.
commands.why: Real accounts with their own home directories.

commands.what: Sets the owning group of the directory.
commands.where: On the shared and admin directories.
commands.why: Group ownership is what setgid passes on to new files.

commands.what: Sets rwx for owner and group, nothing for others, plus the setgid bit.
commands.where: On the shared and admin directories.
commands.why: New files inherit the group; outsiders get no access.

commands.what: Sets a default ACL that new files in the directory inherit.
commands.why: Group stays writable even if a user has umask 077.

commands.what: Shows the directory itself, not its content.
commands.why: `drwxrws---` means setgid is active (the `s`).

sections.tip: A capital `S` in `drwxr-S---` means setgid is set but the group has no execute bit; fix the mode.
sections.warn: Never fix permission problems with `chmod 777`. Everybody could then change or delete the files.

sections.title: 3. Web site with nginx, SELinux and AppArmor
body: Install nginx and let it serve `/srv/company/web`. We add a server block named `company.local` in `/etc/nginx/conf.d/company.conf` (works on both families) and test with a `Host:` header, so the default site does not interfere.

**RHEL/Rocky:** SELinux labels every file. A new directory under `/srv` gets a generic label, so nginx gets **403 Forbidden** although the Unix permissions are fine. The fix is the right label: `semanage fcontext` stores the rule, `restorecon` applies it. Do not use `setenforce 0` as a shortcut; that switches protection off for the whole system.

**Debian/Ubuntu:** there is no label to set. AppArmor is active but nginx is normally not confined by a profile; you only check the status with `aa-status`. A 403 there is a normal permission problem (check the directory modes up to `/srv`).

commands.what: Installs nginx (RHEL, Rocky, Alma). On Ubuntu use `sudo apt install -y nginx`.
commands.where: First step of the web chapter.
commands.why: Package manager handles files and dependencies.

commands.what: Stores a rule: files below web get the web-content label.
commands.why: The label survives a relabel; `chcon` does not.

commands.what: Applies the stored label rule to existing files.
commands.why: Without it the rule exists but files keep the old label.

commands.what: Shows the SELinux label of the directory.
commands.why: You want to see `httpd_sys_content_t`.

commands.what: Tests the nginx configuration without restarting.
commands.why: A typo would otherwise take the site down.

sections.tip: To see why SELinux blocked something: `sudo ausearch -m avc -ts recent`. Read the log before you change anything.
sections.warn: `setenforce 0` is a diagnosis tool at best, never a fix. Label the files instead.

sections.title: 4. Firewall: open 80 and 443, keep SSH
body: RHEL/Rocky uses **firewalld**, Ubuntu uses **ufw**. Both can block you out of your own server when you are connected over SSH. Rules: keep SSH allowed, test with a **runtime** rule first, make it **permanent** only after the test.
firewalld: rules without `--permanent` vanish at reload or reboot; with `--timeout=300` they remove themselves. ufw: rules are saved at once, so allow SSH **before** `ufw enable`.
Always keep a **second SSH session open** (or the VM console) while you change the firewall. If the new rules lock you out, the open session or the console still works.

commands.what: Lists the services allowed in the active zone.
commands.why: Confirms that `ssh` is still there.

commands.what: Stores permanent rules for ports 80 and 443.
commands.why: Survives reload and reboot; apply with `--reload`.

commands.what: Allows SSH (port 22) in ufw.
commands.why: Prevents the lockout when the firewall is switched on.

commands.what: Allows HTTP; repeat with `443/tcp` for HTTPS.
commands.why: Opens only the ports the site needs.

commands.what: Lists listening TCP/UDP ports with the process.
commands.where: To see what the server really offers.
commands.why: Every unexpected port is a finding for your report.

sections.danger: Never remove the `ssh` service or deny port 22 while connected over SSH. Check `--list-services` or `ufw status` for ssh **before** `firewall-cmd --reload` or `ufw enable`. Use the VM console if you are locked out, and restore the snapshot if needed.
sections.tip: Practise reading `ss` output in the simulator: the audit files in your home directory contain a sample listing you can analyse with `grep` and `cut`.

sections.title: 5. Backup script and systemd timer
body: The backup is a short script (modules 6.5/6.6) that writes a dated `tar.gz` archive of `shared`, `web` and `admin` to `/srv/company/backup` and deletes archives older than 7 days. A second disk or remote copy is better in real life; a local folder is enough for the project.

systemd runs the script: a `.service` of `Type=oneshot` describes what to run, a `.timer` describes when (`OnCalendar=`, `Persistent=true`). Enable the **timer**, not the service. After creating or changing unit files run `systemctl daemon-reload`.

On RHEL/Rocky a script in `/srv/company/scripts` has a generic label and systemd may refuse to run it (status 203/EXEC). Give it the label `bin_t` with `semanage fcontext` and `restorecon`, like you did for the web directory.

commands.what: Creates a compressed archive.
commands.why: One dated file per backup is easy to store and restore.

commands.what: Makes systemd read new or changed unit files.
commands.where: After writing the service and timer.
commands.why: Otherwise systemd does not know the new units.

commands.what: Enables the timer at boot and starts it now.
commands.why: The backup then runs every night without you.

commands.what: Shows timers with next and last run.
commands.why: You see when the next backup will run.

commands.what: Makes the script executable.
commands.why: Without the x bit the service cannot start it.

sections.danger: `find ... -delete` cannot be undone. Test the line with `-print` instead of `-delete` first and run it only on `/srv/company/backup`.
sections.tip: Run the service once by hand with `sudo systemctl start company-backup.service` and look at `ls -l /srv/company/backup` before you wait for the timer.

sections.title: 6. Verification checklist and delivery report
body: A server is only finished when you have **proof**. Go through the checklist: users and groups, setgid shared directory, site answers with 200, SELinux label or AppArmor status, firewall has ssh/80/443, timer is enabled, a backup file exists, backup directory is `700`.

A small script prints `OK:` or `FAIL:` per check, so the result is easy to read and to paste. The **delivery report** `/srv/company/REPORT.txt` contains host, date, the verification output and the listening ports. This is what you hand over.
If a line says FAIL, go back to that chapter and fix it. Do not edit the report by hand to hide a failure.

commands.what: Shows the group entry with members.
commands.why: Reads from the real user database.

commands.what: Prints permissions, owner and group in one line.
commands.where: In checks and in the report.
commands.why: Short proof that the mode is `drwxrws---`.

commands.what: Fetches only the HTTP headers.
commands.where: To test the web site locally.
commands.why: `200 OK` shows nginx answered the local request and content permissions/labels allow access; check firewall rules separately and, if possible, test from another machine.

commands.what: Counts lines.
commands.where: To check that the report is not empty.
commands.why: A report needs real content.

sections.tip: Run the checklist after a reboot, too. A service that works only until the next reboot is not finished.

t01.text: Create the project root in your home directory: `mkdir -p ~/srv/company` (in the VM this is `/srv/company`).

t02.text: Create the five subdirectories `shared`, `admin`, `web`, `backup` and `scripts` inside `~/srv/company` with one `mkdir` command.

t03.text: Set a strict umask for the project work: `umask 027`.
t03.hint: 027 removes all rights for others and write for the group on new files.

t04.text: Give the shared directory mode `2770` (setgid, rwx for owner and group, nothing for others).

t05.text: Make `web` readable for everybody (`755`) and `backup` private (`700`).

t06.text:
Write the site page: put the text `

Small Company

` into `~/srv/company/web/index.html`.
t06.hint: Use `echo "..." > file`; quote the text because of the `<` and `>` characters.

t07.text: Write the nginx server block to `~/srv/company/company.conf`: lines `server {`, `listen 80;`, `server_name company.local;`, `root /srv/company/web;` and `}`.
t07.hint: `printf` with `\n` writes several lines at once; put the text in single quotes.

t08.text: Predict: which permission string will `ls -ld ~/srv/company/shared` show? Write it down, then run the command.

t09.text: Predict: which members does the group `admins` have in `~/audit/group.txt`? Run `grep admins ~/audit/group.txt | cut -d: -f4` to confirm.
t09.hint: Field 4 of the group file is the member list.

t10.text: Predict: how many lines in `~/audit/ss.txt` contain `LISTEN`? Check with `grep -c LISTEN ~/audit/ss.txt`.

t11.text: Debug: the test site in `~/srv/site` would give nginx a 403. The directory has mode `700` and `index.html` has `600`. Fix them to `755` and `644`.

t12.text: Debug: `~/srv/broken/backup.sh` fails with Permission denied. Fix it and run it so that `~/srv/broken/out/notes.bak` exists.
t12.hint: The script needs the x bit: `chmod 755`, then run it with its path.

t13.text: Mini project: write `~/srv/company/scripts/backup.sh` with the line `#!/bin/bash` and a `cp` line that copies `~/srv/company/web/index.html` to `~/srv/company/backup/index.html.bak`. Make it executable and run it.

t14.text: Mini project: write the unit files `company-backup.service` (`Type=oneshot`, `ExecStart=/srv/company/scripts/backup.sh`) and `company-backup.timer` (`[Timer]`, `OnCalendar=*-*-* 02:00:00`, `Persistent=true`, `[Install]`, `WantedBy=timers.target`) into `~/srv/company/scripts`.
t14.hint: Two `printf` commands with `\n`; the service needs `[Unit]` and `[Service]`, the timer needs `[Unit]`, `[Timer]` and `[Install]`.

t15.text: Challenge: write the firewall plan `~/srv/company/firewall-plan.txt`, one command per line, in a safe order: `firewall-cmd --permanent --add-service=` for ssh first, then http, then https, and finally `firewall-cmd --reload`.
t15.hint: Start the file with `>`, then add lines with `>>`. SSH must come first.

t16.text: Challenge: write the delivery report `~/srv/company/REPORT.txt` with at least 8 lines: title, host name (use `$(hostname)`), date, users alice bob carol, groups staff admins, shared directory, web ports 80 and 443, backup.
t16.hint: Start with `echo "..." > file`, add lines with `>>`. `echo "Host: $(hostname)"` fills in the host.

t17.text: Ticket: The auditor says the server may listen on unexpected ports. Use `~/audit/ss.txt` and write all lines whose port is not 22, 80 or 443 into `~/audit/unexpected.txt`.
t17.hint: `grep -v -E ':(22|80|443) ' file > result`; the space after the closing bracket matters.

t18.text: Ticket: Management wants the team list. From `~/audit/passwd.txt` write the names of the real users (home directory under `/home/`) sorted into `~/audit/team.txt`, one per line.

vm.intro: Do the real project in your VM, in this order. First take a snapshot: if anything fails, you go back. Paste the output when a task asks for it. Commands marked for RHEL or Ubuntu: run only your variant.

v01.title: Snapshot and starting state
v01.text: Take a VM snapshot named `before-company-project` in your VM program (module 0.2). Then check the system and paste the output.

blocks.cmd:
grep -E '^(ID|PRETTY_NAME)=' /etc/os-release
# RHEL / Rocky / Alma:
getenforce
# Debian / Ubuntu:
sudo aa-status | head -n 3

differs: `getenforce: command not found` on Ubuntu is normal; use the `aa-status` line.
If SELinux says Permissive or Disabled, tell your teacher/notes; continue but do not change the mode with `setenforce`.

v02.title: Users, groups, shared directory
v02.text: Create groups, users and the directory tree with setgid. Then prove it and paste the output.

blocks.cmd:
sudo groupadd staff
sudo groupadd admins
for u in alice bob carol; do sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash -G staff $u; done
sudo usermod -aG admins alice
sudo mkdir -p /srv/company/{shared,admin,web,backup,scripts}
sudo chgrp staff /srv/company/shared
sudo chgrp admins /srv/company/admin
sudo chmod 2770 /srv/company/shared /srv/company/admin
sudo chmod 755 /srv/company/web
sudo chmod 750 /srv/company/scripts
sudo chmod 700 /srv/company/backup

sudo -u bob touch /srv/company/shared/from_bob.txt
ls -ld /srv/company/shared
ls -l /srv/company/shared
getent group staff
id alice
sudo -u carol ls /srv/company/admin
blocks.expected:
drwxrws--- 2 root staff 4096 ... /srv/company/shared
-rw-r--r-- 1 bob staff 0 ... from_bob.txt
staff:x:1002:alice,bob,carol
uid=1001(alice) gid=1001(alice) groups=1001(alice),1002(staff),1003(admins)
ls: cannot open directory '/srv/company/admin': Permission denied

differs: Group ids differ between systems; only the names must match.
If `from_bob.txt` has group `bob` instead of `staff`, the setgid bit is missing: repeat `chmod 2770`.
Optional default ACL (install package `acl` first): `sudo setfacl -d -m g:staff:rwx /srv/company/shared`.

v03.title: Web site with the right label
v03.text: Install nginx, add the server block and the page, test, fix the label (RHEL) or check AppArmor (Ubuntu) and paste the last curl output.

blocks.cmd:
# RHEL / Rocky / Alma:
sudo dnf install -y nginx policycoreutils-python-utils
# Debian / Ubuntu:
sudo apt install -y nginx

blocks.expected:
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden   (RHEL before the label fix)
HTTP/1.1 200 OK          (Ubuntu)

blocks.cmd:
# RHEL / Rocky / Alma only:
ls -Zd /srv/company/web
sudo semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_sys_content_t "/srv/company/web(/.*)?"
sudo restorecon -Rv /srv/company/web
ls -Zd /srv/company/web
# Debian / Ubuntu only:
sudo aa-status | grep -i nginx
# both:
curl -sI -H 'Host: company.local' http://localhost | head -n 1
curl -s -H 'Host: company.local' http://localhost

differs: 403 after the label fix on RHEL: check `ls -Zd` again and the modes of `/srv` and `/srv/company` (they need `x` for others).
Connection refused: `sudo systemctl status nginx`; port 80 may be used by another service (`ss -tulpn`).

v04.title: Firewall without lockout
v04.text: Keep a second SSH session or the console open. Allow web ports without losing SSH, then paste the rule list.

blocks.cmd:
# RHEL / Rocky / Alma (firewalld):
sudo firewall-cmd --list-services
sudo firewall-cmd --add-service={http,https} --timeout=300
curl -sI http://localhost | head -n 1
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-service={http,https}
sudo firewall-cmd --reload
sudo firewall-cmd --list-services

# Debian / Ubuntu (ufw): SSH FIRST!
sudo ufw allow OpenSSH
sudo ufw allow 80/tcp
sudo ufw allow 443/tcp
sudo ufw enable
sudo ufw status
blocks.expected:
Status: active
OpenSSH                    ALLOW       Anywhere
80/tcp                     ALLOW       Anywhere
443/tcp                    ALLOW       Anywhere

differs: No `ssh` in the list on RHEL: add it at once with `sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-service=ssh` and reload.
`ufw: command not found` on Rocky is fine; you use firewalld there.
Locked out? Use the VM console, or restore the snapshot.

v05.title: Backup script and timer
v05.text: Create the backup script and the systemd units, enable the timer, run one backup by hand and paste the timer list.

blocks.cmd:
sudo tee /srv/company/scripts/backup.sh >/dev/null <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
DEST=/srv/company/backup
tar -czf "$DEST/company-$(date +%F_%H%M).tar.gz" -C /srv/company shared web admin
find "$DEST" -name 'company-*.tar.gz' -mtime +7 -delete
EOF
sudo chmod 750 /srv/company/scripts/backup.sh

sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/company-backup.service >/dev/null <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Company backup

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/srv/company/scripts/backup.sh
EOF
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/company-backup.timer >/dev/null <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Daily company backup

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 02:00:00
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF

# RHEL / Rocky / Alma only (script label):
sudo semanage fcontext -a -t bin_t "/srv/company/scripts(/.*)?"
sudo restorecon -Rv /srv/company/scripts
# both:
sudo systemd-analyze verify /etc/systemd/system/company-backup.service
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now company-backup.timer
sudo systemctl start company-backup.service
sudo ls -l /srv/company/backup
systemctl list-timers company-backup.timer --no-pager
blocks.expected:
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 2048 ... company-2026-11-12_0215.tar.gz
NEXT                        LEFT   LAST PASSED UNIT                 ACTIVATES
Fri 2026-11-13 02:00:00 CET 23h    -    -      company-backup.timer company-backup.service

differs: `status=203/EXEC` in `systemctl status company-backup.service`: on RHEL set the `bin_t` label (first lines of this block) and check the x bit.
Do not test the `find ... -delete` line on other directories; if in doubt replace `-delete` with `-print`.
If the timer is not listed, you probably forgot `daemon-reload`.

v06.title: Verification checklist and delivery report
v06.text: Write the checklist script, run it as root and build the delivery report. All lines must say OK. Paste the verify output.

blocks.cmd:
sudo tee /srv/company/scripts/verify.sh >/dev/null <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
set -o pipefail
chk() { local label=$1; shift; if "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "OK: $label"; else echo "FAIL: $label"; fi; }
staff_ok() { id -nG alice | grep -qw staff && id -nG bob | grep -qw staff && id -nG carol | grep -qw staff; }
site_ok() { curl -fsS -H 'Host: company.local' http://localhost | grep -q Company; }
selinux_ok() { if ! command -v getenforce >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ "$(getenforce)" = Disabled ]; then return 0; fi; ls -Zd /srv/company/web | grep -q httpd_sys_content_t; }
firewall_ok() {
  if command -v firewall-cmd >/dev/null 2>&1 && firewall-cmd --state >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    local services
    services=$(firewall-cmd --list-services) || return 1
    for service in ssh http https; do [[ " $services " == *" $service "* ]] || return 1; done
  elif command -v ufw >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    local status
    status=$(ufw status) || return 1
    grep -q '^Status: active' <<<"$status" && grep -Eq '^OpenSSH[[:space:]]+ALLOW' <<<"$status" && grep -Eq '^80/tcp[[:space:]]+ALLOW' <<<"$status" && grep -Eq '^443/tcp[[:space:]]+ALLOW' <<<"$status"
  else
    return 1
  fi
}
backup_ok() { compgen -G '/srv/company/backup/company-*.tar.gz' >/dev/null; }
backup_mode_ok() { [[ $(stat -c %a /srv/company/backup) == 700 ]]; }
chk "alice bob carol are in staff" staff_ok
chk "shared has setgid" test -g /srv/company/shared
chk "site answers with Small Company" site_ok
chk "nginx enabled" systemctl is-enabled --quiet nginx
chk "web label (SELinux) or no SELinux" selinux_ok
chk "firewall allows SSH, HTTP and HTTPS" firewall_ok
chk "timer enabled" systemctl is-enabled --quiet company-backup.timer
chk "backup archive exists" backup_ok
chk "backup dir is 700" backup_mode_ok
EOF
sudo bash /srv/company/scripts/verify.sh
blocks.expected:
OK: alice bob carol are in staff
OK: shared has setgid
OK: site answers with Small Company
OK: nginx enabled
OK: web label (SELinux) or no SELinux
OK: firewall allows SSH, HTTP and HTTPS
OK: timer enabled
OK: backup archive exists
OK: backup dir is 700

blocks.cmd:
{ echo "Company server delivery report"; echo "Host: $(hostname)"; echo "Date: $(date)"; echo "--- verification ---"; sudo bash /srv/company/scripts/verify.sh; echo "--- listening ports ---"; ss -tulpn; } | sudo tee /srv/company/REPORT.txt
wc -l /srv/company/REPORT.txt

differs: Any `FAIL:` line: go back to the matching chapter, fix it and run the script again.
The `[ ... = 700 ]` line needs the backslash before `$(stat` exactly as written, otherwise the shell expands it too early.
Finally reboot and run the verify script again: everything must still be OK.

q1.q: On Rocky Linux nginx returns 403 for files in /srv/company/web although the mode is 755. What is the most likely cause?
options: The files carry the wrong SELinux label (not httpd_sys_content_t)
Port 80 is closed in the firewall
q1.explain: A closed port gives a timeout, not a 403. A generic label under /srv blocks nginx; fix it with semanage fcontext and restorecon, not with setenforce 0.

q2.q: You are connected over SSH to an Ubuntu server. What is the safe way to switch on ufw?
options: ufw enable first, then add rules
ufw allow OpenSSH first, then ufw enable
Disable SSH and use the console
q2.explain: ufw rules are active at once. Without an allowed SSH rule, enabling the firewall cuts your session.

q3.q: Why does the shared directory get mode 2770 (setgid)?
options: New files inherit the group staff, so the team can work on each other's files
q3.explain: The setgid bit on a directory passes its group to new files. 770 keeps others out.

q4.q: You created company-backup.service and company-backup.timer. What must you do so the nightly backup runs?
options: systemctl daemon-reload, then systemctl enable --now company-backup.timer
q4.explain: systemd must re-read unit files (daemon-reload), and the timer unit has to be enabled and started; the service is started by the timer.

summary: Plan first, take a VM snapshot, work only in the test VM.
Shared directory: group staff, mode 2770 (setgid), least privilege elsewhere: web 755, scripts 750, backup 700.
nginx on RHEL needs the label httpd_sys_content_t (semanage fcontext + restorecon); on Ubuntu you check AppArmor.
Firewall: keep ssh, test with runtime rules or --timeout, keep a second session; ufw: allow OpenSSH before enable.
Backup: script + service (oneshot) + timer; daemon-reload, enable --now the timer; on RHEL label the script bin_t.
Finish with a checklist (OK/FAIL) and a delivery report file as proof.

glossary.meaning: A saved state of the VM you can return to if a step goes wrong.
New files inherit the directory's group instead of the creator's primary group.
An access rule on a directory that new files inherit.
A security context (such as httpd_sys_content_t) on files; decides what a process may access.
Stores a permanent file-label rule; restorecon applies it.
Path-based security system of Debian/Ubuntu; checked with aa-status.
Firewall front ends of RHEL-family and Ubuntu systems.
Runtime rules vanish at reload or reboot; permanent rules are stored.
A unit that starts a service on a schedule (OnCalendar=).
The file that documents the finished server and the verification results.
